questions.question: A sign states a maximum total weight. How does that limit apply to a car towing a trailer?
options: It applies to the combined weight of car and trailer
It applies to each of the connected vehicles separately
It applies only to the towing vehicle
It applies only to the trailer and its load
questions.explanation: For connected vehicles the stated figure is read per vehicle, so each unit of the combination must stay below it. A separate sign exists for the combined weight of connected vehicles.

questions.question: Besides banning a left turn, what else does a no-left-turn sign forbid at that junction?
options: Turning around in a U-turn
Turning right into the side road
Stopping anywhere inside the junction
Overtaking on the approach to it
questions.explanation: A U-turn is treated as a left turn taken to its extreme, so the sign covers it without any separate no-U-turn sign being posted.

questions.question: Over what stretch of road is a no-U-turn sign valid?
options: Only at the point where the sign is placed
Until an end-of-prohibition sign is passed
Along the whole street the sign stands on
Up to and including the next crossing
questions.explanation: The ban covers the road ahead as far as the next crossing, and the crossing itself is included, so turning around in it is still forbidden.

questions.question: What exactly does the ordinary no-overtaking sign prohibit?
options: Overtaking any vehicle, cycles included
Overtaking motor vehicles with more than two wheels
Overtaking only goods vehicles and buses
Overtaking anything other than a stopped vehicle
questions.explanation: The prohibition is defined by what is being passed: motor vehicles running on more than two wheels. A separate sign restricts goods vehicles from overtaking.

questions.question: What background colour does a destination sign with distances carry outside urban areas?
options: Green
Yellow
White
Blue
questions.explanation: Rural destination signs use a yellow background, while the same information inside urban areas is shown on a white or a blue background.

questions.question: A supplementary plate reading "200 m" is fitted under a prohibition sign. What does the figure state?
options: The distance to the place where the sign must be obeyed
The length of road over which the prohibition runs
The distance to the next sign of the same kind
The distance over which stopping is still permitted
questions.explanation: A single distance tells you how far ahead the danger or the point of obedience lies. A plate showing two figures, such as 200-800 m, is the one that gives both distance and length of the zone.

questions.question: A road is signed as a "difficult road". Which vehicles is it meant for?
options: Any private car driven at reduced speed
Vehicles higher than ordinary cars and with four-wheel drive
Only specially equipped off-road vehicles
Any vehicle carrying recovery equipment
questions.explanation: Difficult roads call for a jeep-type vehicle with extra ground clearance and four-wheel drive. Tracks that demand specially equipped off-road vehicles carry the stronger "very rough track" sign instead.

questions.question: How are the reflectors on left and right roadside markers arranged?
options: They point diagonally towards the road
They point diagonally away from the road
They face straight along the line of the road
They face directly across the carriageway
questions.explanation: Angling the reflectors inwards throws the headlight beam back to an approaching driver, which is what makes the edge of the road readable in the dark.

questions.question: On a half broken centre line, how do the painted segments compare with the gaps?
options: The segments are three times as long as the gaps
The segments and the gaps are equally long
The gaps are three times as long as the segments
The segments are twice as long as the gaps
questions.explanation: Long paint and short gaps is the visual warning that overtaking here is dangerous and demands extreme care. Equal paint and gaps is the pattern of a broken side line.

questions.question: The centre marking beside your lane is broken while the line on the far side is continuous. What applies?
options: Neither direction of traffic may overtake here
Both directions may overtake if it is done with care
You may overtake, but oncoming traffic may not
You may not overtake, but oncoming traffic may
questions.explanation: Each direction obeys the line nearest to it, so the broken line permits your overtaking while the continuous line bars it for the other side.

questions.question: An unbroken yellow line runs along the edge of the road. What does it mean?
options: Parking is barred, but a brief stop is allowed
Only loading and unloading are permitted there
Parking is reserved for permit holders only
Stopping a vehicle at that location is prohibited
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line is the stronger of the two: it bans stopping altogether. A broken yellow line is the one that bans parking only.

questions.question: How is a parking bay reserved for special vehicles such as delivery vans marked out?
options: With the usual bay lines plus diagonals joining opposite corners
With the usual bay lines drawn in yellow instead of white
With the usual bay lines plus a line closing the entrance
With the usual bay lines drawn at double the normal width
questions.explanation: The bay keeps the ordinary 50-100 mm line segments and adds a cross of diagonals between the corners to flag its restricted use.

questions.question: A police officer controlling traffic holds an arm straight out to the side. What must you do if you are approaching from the front?
options: Stop and wait for further instructions
Carry on, as the signal covers the side roads
Slow down and pass behind the officer
Stop only if another vehicle is crossing
questions.explanation: The outstretched arm halts traffic coming from in front of and from behind the officer, while road users approaching from the side may keep moving.

questions.question: A traffic light shows red and amber together. What does that combination mean?
options: Move off, since green is about to show
Cross the junction, but proceed with caution
Stop, because the light is about to turn green
Stop, because the light is about to turn red
questions.explanation: It carries the full force of the red light, and the amber only forewarns of the change, so the junction may not be entered yet.

questions.question: The main light is green and a separate left-arrow light stands beside it. When may you turn left?
options: As soon as the main green light comes on
While the main light shows red and amber
Whenever there is no oncoming traffic
Only once the left arrow itself is lit
questions.explanation: Where a directional arrow is provided, it governs that turn, so the green main light alone is not authority to make it.

questions.question: Several pedestrian lights at one crossing face the same direction. Which one must a pedestrian obey?
options: The one on the far side of the carriageway
The one mounted on the vehicle traffic light
The one standing closest to the pedestrian
Whichever of them is currently showing green
questions.explanation: The nearest light governs the section of carriageway immediately in front of the pedestrian, so a further light may already be releasing a different stage.

questions.question: A red light flashing on and off is mounted across a road section. What is required of you?
options: Pass the signal with extra caution
Give way to traffic coming from the right
Stop only when an emergency vehicle is in sight
Stop before the stop line, or before the signal itself
questions.explanation: The flashing red closes the section, for instance where emergency vehicles pull out or aircraft cross low. Only a driver already too close to halt safely should carry on past it.
